record.paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
record.context_brief: One-quarter class analogue of Blumenthal theorem
record.original_question: Let {P_n(x)} be an orthogonal polynomial sequence defined by P_n(x) = (x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x) - λ_n P_{n-2}(x) for n ≥ 1, with P_{-1}(x)=0, P_0(x)=1, each c_n real, each λ_n > 0, c_n → ∞, and λ_{n+1}/(c_n c_{n+1}) → 1/4. If x_{n,1} < \cdots < x_{n,n} are the zeros of P_n, ξ_i = lim_{n→∞} x_{n,i}, η_j = lim_{n→∞} x_{n,n-j+1}, σ = lim_{i→∞} ξ_i, and τ = lim_{j→∞} η_j, then in the difficult one-quarter-class case σ = -∞ and τ = ∞, is there an analogue of Blumenthal's theorem describing the limiting distribution of the zeros for this unbounded situation?

evidence.quote: We would like to ﬁnd analogues of these theorems when the sequences above are unbounded. To this end, let us consider the “one quarter class” of orthogonal polynomials (see [10]); namely, let lim n→∞ cn = ∞, and lim n→∞ λn+1/(cncn+1) = 1/4. ... This now leaves the most diﬃcult case, σ = −∞. We thus pose the inevitable question: Is there an analog of Blumenthal’s theorem for this case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{P_n(x)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a sequence of monic orthogonal polynomials defined by the three-term recurrence
\[ P_n(x) = (x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x) - \lambda_n P_{n-2}(x), \quad n\ge 1, \]
with $P_{-1}(x)=0$ and $P_0(x)=1$, where $c_n\in\mathbb R$, $\lambda_n>0$ for all $n$, and the recurrence coefficients satisfy
\[ \lim_{n\to\infty} c_n = \infty, \qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\lambda_{n+1}}{c_n c_{n+1}} = \frac{1}{4} \]
(the "one-quarter class"). Let $x_{n,1}<x_{n,2}<\cdots<x_{n,n}$ be the zeros of $P_n$. Define
\[ \xi_i = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n,i},\quad \eta_j = \lim_{n\to\infty} x_{n,n-j+1},\quad \sigma=\lim_{i\to\infty}\xi_i,\quad \tau=\lim_{j\to\infty}\eta_j, \]
and assume one is in the case $\sigma=-\infty$ and $\tau=+\infty$. Provide an analogue of Blumenthal's theorem for this situation: namely, describe the limiting distribution / closure of the set of zeros $\bigcup_{n,i}\{x_{n,i}\}$ of the polynomials $P_n$ in $\mathbb R$ in this unbounded one-quarter-class case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the OPSFA13 open problems session. A related case ($\sigma$ finite, $\tau=\infty$) was addressed by Świderski, who showed under a monotonicity assumption that $[\sigma,\infty)$ is the essential spectrum, but the doubly unbounded case $\sigma=-\infty$, $\tau=\infty$ remains the most difficult and no analogue of Blumenthal's theorem covering it appears to have been established.

status_evidence.snippet: This now leaves the most difficult case, σ = −∞. We thus pose the inevitable question: Is there an analog of Blumenthal's theorem for this case?
status_evidence.claim: The case σ = −∞ is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Blumenthal–Nevai theorems for the one quarter class of orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Świderski proved that with a slight monotonicity condition, [σ, ∞) is the essential spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for the case with σ finite, but not for σ = −∞.
